sections.h2: Where do Richardson homeowners pay property tax?
sections.html:
Richardson property owners pay at the county tax office for the county where the house sits, because the city straddles Dallas County and Collin County. The city's property tax page says plainly that taxes must be paid at that county office, and it lists both.

  • Dallas County Tax Office: 6820 LBJ Freeway, Dallas, TX 75240, 214-653-7811.
  • Collin County Tax Office: 900 E. Park Blvd, Ste 100, Plano, TX 75074, 972-881-3014.
  • Dallas Central Appraisal District: 2949 N. Stemmons Freeway, Dallas, 214-631-0910, for values and exemptions on Dallas County parcels.
  • Collin Central Appraisal District: 250 Eldorado Pkwy, McKinney, 469-742-9200, for the Collin County side.

The city's FAQ gives the rhythm of the year. Bills are issued in October and do not turn delinquent until February 1 of the following year, so the 2026 tax is billed in October 2026 and becomes delinquent on February 1, 2027.

sections.h2: What is the Richardson city tax rate?
sections.html:
The city council adopted the 2026-27 budget with the property tax rate held at $0.54218 per $100 of assessed valuation. The city's September 25, 2026 news release says the budget also continues a $160,000 exemption for seniors, and its budget is $432,226,829.

City of Richardson estimate of the typical homeowner's city-side costs, as printed in the 2026-27 budget announcement
ItemFY 2025-26FY 2026-27
Average taxable value of a homestead$411,065$424,062
Property tax, city portion$2,229$2,299
Water charges$1,171$1,231
Sewer charges$616$691
Drainage fee$74$86
Residential solid waste$332$344

The release explains that the rate did not change, but a higher average taxable value moves the city share of the bill up by about $70 a year. It also notes new water and wastewater rates from October 1, with the monthly base charge on a 3/4-inch meter rising from $8 to $9.60.

The city describes the budget as a continuation of a multi-year plan to protect essential services, strengthen its workforce and keep investing in public safety, infrastructure and economic development. It also adds employee pay adjustments and continued work on voter-approved bond projects. Those priorities are what the tax rate pays for, alongside water, sewer, drainage and trash fees that appear on separate city bills.

These figures cover the city only. Richardson ISD, the county and any other unit send their own charges through the county tax office.

sections.h2: Does Richardson offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Richardson does not offer the optional percentage homestead exemption, so nothing appears for it on the city's line of a Collin or Dallas County statement. The city's FAQ explains that only school districts must grant a homestead exemption, and that other units choose whether to adopt an optional one.

The city does give a senior exemption, which the budget release puts at $160,000. Apply through the appraisal district for the county where your property lies, not through city hall. The state-level breaks sit on top of that:

  • Richardson ISD, like every school district, must give the $140,000 residence homestead exemption.
  • An owner 65 or older, or disabled, gets an extra $60,000 on school tax.
  • The appraised value of a homestead cannot rise more than 10 percent in a year after the first qualifying year.
  • Applications are due before May 1, though a buyer who closes after January 1 can claim the rest of the year if the seller held no exemption.
  • A veteran with a 100 percent VA rating gets a full exemption on the residence homestead.

sections.h2: What penalties apply to late Richardson property tax?
sections.html:
The penalty starts the day after January 31. On February 1 the collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest. The penalty climbs one percent a month until July 1, when it becomes 12 percent, and interest continues at one percent a month with no cap. A unit that hires a private attorney may add up to 20 percent.

Owners who want to spread payment can pay half by November 30 and half by June 30. A 65-or-older or disabled homestead owner can use four installments, with a six percent penalty on a late installment. A collector may waive penalty and interest if payment arrives within 21 days of the owner learning of the delinquency and the written request comes before the 181st day.

An appraisal protest runs separately. File by May 15, or 30 days after the notice was delivered if that is later. Pay at least the undisputed tax before February 1 while the dispute continues.

sections.h2: How does unpaid tax affect selling a Richardson house?
sections.html:
Taxes are a lien from January 1, so they stay with the property through a sale. A title company will ask for delinquent amounts to be paid at closing, since a buyer cannot get clear title until they are. The person who owned on January 1 also remains liable for that year's bill.

Utility accounts matter at the same time. Richardson's utility customer service line is 972-744-4120, and the 2026-27 budget changed the way residential wastewater is calculated, using only the prior year's November through February water use and leaving out the highest month. A seller who is closing should call utility customer service about ending the account so the final bill is settled. Customers over 65 with a 3/4-inch or 1-inch meter keep the old $8 base charge.

Street work can touch a listing too. The city reported sanitary sewer rehabilitation near the Promenade Shopping Center off Coit Road and in the Berkner Park neighborhood, using pipe bursting and pipe lining so that road closures stay minor and fewer construction vehicles are needed.

If the taxing unit has sued and sold the house, the former owner of a homestead has two years after the buyer's deed is filed to redeem, while other property has 180 days. Heirs who inherit a Richardson house should record the right paperwork before selling, such as a muniment of title order, an executor's deed, or an affidavit of death with a transfer on death deed.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Richardson?
sections.html:
Richardson covers 28.57 square miles of land and had 119,469 residents in the 2020 Census. The July 2025 estimate is 118,542, which is 0.8 percent below the 2020 base. The 2020 density works out to about 4,182 people per square mile.

Owners live in just 50.7 percent of homes. The median owned home is valued at $431,400 for 2020-2024, median gross rent is $1,857, and median household income is $98,111. Some 57.0 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and the average commute is 23.6 minutes. The city counted 45,818 households at 2.48 people each, and 79.0 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Median monthly costs for owners with a mortgage are $2,524.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay Richardson property tax to?
faqs.a: Pay the county tax office where the house sits. Richardson reaches into both Dallas County and Collin County, and the city's website lists the office address and phone for each.

faqs.q: What is Richardson's property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's 2026-27 rate is $0.54218 per $100 of assessed valuation, held unchanged by the budget the council adopted. Richardson ISD, the county and other units add their own rates.

faqs.q: Does Richardson have a senior exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's budget announcement says the $160,000 senior property tax exemption continues in 2026-27. Ask the appraisal district for your county how to apply.

faqs.q: When does Richardson property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1 of the year after the tax year. The city's FAQ gives the example of 2026 tax billed in October 2026 and delinquent on February 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Richardson house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent tax is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing so the title is clear. The owner on January 1 stays liable for that year's tax, so the closing statement should say who pays which part.
